newsitem.title: USA: Kodak names new chiefs for consumer imaging business.
newsitem.headline: Kodak names new chiefs for consumer imaging business.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co. named new co-chief operating officers for its Consumer Imaging business, in an attempt to improve its global focus and worldwide strategies, the company said Wednesday.

Analysts said the move is likely an effort to shake up Kodak's largest business following recent lackluster performance and concerns that it is on the losing end of a "price war" in the U.S. photo film market with its biggest rival, Fuji Photo Film Co. Ltd.
Henri Petit and Patrick Siewert were appointed to lead the unit.
Current Consumer Imaging COO Alexander Wasilov will exchange positions with Siewert, and become head of the company's Greater China Region, Kodak said.
Stewart and Petit will report to David Biehn, president of Consumer Imaging. Petit currently heads the company's operations in its European, African and Middle Eastern Region.

"I think it is very likely that (Kodak) is not satisfied with the performance (of the unit) as of late and is changing players in an effort to right the ship, provide fresh perspective and achieve better performance," one analyst said.
"Though I think this business with Fuji is somewhat exaggerated, the fact remains that the stock has taken a hit, and (Kodak) may believe it's time to make a change."
Kodak's stock, off 62.5 cents at $76.8125 in late morning trading, is down from a 12-month high of $94.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Nine days ago, Kodak said it was dropping long-time ad agency J. Walter Thompson and assigning all product and service advertising for its Consumer Imaging business to Ogilvy & Mather, Worldwide, as of July 1.
